domains.name: Auto-Moderation
domains.promise: Every guild message is scanned against owner-configured automod rules (word, link, invite, spam, duplicate, caps, mention-spam, and newline filters) under hard per-regex and per-message time budgets that always fail toward no-match; automod ships in observe-only mode that logs would-be violations without touching members or messages, and owner-enabled enforcement explains every action to the member in the owner's voice and remains fully reversible via pardon.

controls.description: Master switch for the automod scanning pipeline; when off no rules are evaluated and configuration is preserved.
Global posture: observe logs each rule match to the mod log without acting on the member or message; enforce executes each rule’s configured action.

Prioritized rule list; each rule carries a type (word_filter, link_filter, invite_filter, spam_filter, duplicate_filter, caps_filter, mention_spam, newline_spam), a type-specific config, an action (delete, warn, mute, kick, ban), exempt roles and channels, and a mod-log flag. Higher priority evaluates first.

constraints.shape: array of { type, config, action, priority, exempt-roles, exempt-channels, log-to-mod-channel }

controls.description: Hard sandboxed-VM timeout for a single owner-authored regex evaluation; a timed-out pattern is skipped and treated as no match so a slow rule can never punish a member.

Aggregate wall-clock budget for evaluating all rules — and all words within a rule — against one message; on exhaustion the remaining rules are skipped with a warning and the message is treated as clean.
Channel receiving automod detections and enforcement entries; empty string disables mod-log posts.

defaults.rationale: Scanning on from day one gives owners visibility at zero member risk because the shipped mode is observe-only.
Lenient locked default: owners watch exactly what automod would do before any member is ever touched, then opt into enforcement deliberately.
Gentle starter set covering the highest-signal abuse shapes; under the observe default it only reports, never acts, and own-server invites stay welcome.
Calibrated bound: firm enough to stop catastrophic backtracking from blocking the event loop, generous enough that legitimate rules never misclassify as timeouts on a loaded host.
Aggregate cap so many rules — or many words inside one owner-editable rule — can never stall message handling; a budget bail always fails toward no match.
No mod-log channel until the owner picks one; the setup flow nudges owners to set it so observe mode has somewhere to report.

domains.name: Infractions & Appeals
domains.promise: Moderation is warn-before-punish: /warn, /mute, /kick, /ban, /pardon, and /infractions record every action as an expiring infraction, escalation follows an owner-tunable chain that always issues pure warnings before the first punishment, every affected member is told what happened, why, and how to appeal in a respectful DM, and appeals filed from Discord or the member portal are reviewed by a human and can reverse any action.

controls.description: Ordered escalation steps mapping an active-infraction threshold to an action (warn, mute with duration, kick, ban) and a DM flag; evaluated against the member’s active, unpardoned infraction count.

constraints.shape: array of { threshold, action, duration-minutes?, dm-member }

controls.description: Days until an active infraction expires, stops counting toward escalation, and is deactivated by the periodic expiry sweep.
Channel receiving moderation action entries with active counts and the next escalation step; empty string disables mod-log posts.
Whether members receive a DM explaining each moderation action; kick and ban DMs are sent before the action so they can still be delivered.
Whether members can appeal infractions via the Discord appeal entry point and the member portal.
Channel where filed appeals are posted for moderator review; empty string falls back to the mod log channel.
Minimum wait before the same infraction can be appealed again after a denial.

defaults.rationale: Warn-before-punish locked default: two pure warnings before the first mute, graduated durations before removal, and every step DMs the member.
Forgiving 30-day memory: old mistakes fall off instead of haunting members toward escalation forever.
No mod-log channel until the owner picks one; the setup flow nudges owners to set it so escalation context is visible.
Member-respectful default: nobody is punished silently — every action explains itself.
Locked decision: every punishment carries an appeal path by default, reachable from both Discord and the member portal.
Appeals land in the mod log until the owner dedicates a review channel, so no appeal is ever invisible.
Guardrail against appeal spam while keeping the path genuinely open — one respectful retry per day per infraction.

permissions.enforcement: Commands register with a Moderate Members default member permission and handlers re-check hierarchy: the bot refuses to act on bots, the invoker themselves, the server owner, or anyone at or above the invoker’s highest role.

permissions.actor: Guild moderator holding Kick Members or Ban Members respectively
permissions.enforcement: Kick and ban register with their matching Discord default member permissions and refuse targets the bot cannot act on, replying with a clear role-hierarchy hint instead of leaking API errors.

permissions.actor: Any member with an active infraction
permissions.action: File one appeal per infraction via the Discord appeal entry point or the member portal
permissions.enforcement: The appeal surface only ever files against the requesting member’s own infractions, enforces the per-infraction appeal cooldown, and never exposes another member’s history.
Discord hides the commands by default, the handler re-checks and replies with an ephemeral denial, appeal resolution requires a moderator session, and every denied attempt writes an audit row.

domains.name: Anti-Raid Protection
domains.promise: Anti-raid ships disabled so calm servers feel zero friction; when the owner enables it, an account-age gate politely defers too-new accounts, a per-guild sliding join window detects floods, and containment is graduated — turning raid-window joiners away first and only escalating to lockdown (verification raised to Very High plus invites paused) if the flood persists — with every measure auto-reversing after the calm cooldown: verification restored, invites recreated, and raid bans automatically lifted.

controls.description: Master switch for anti-raid protection; when off every join flows completely untouched.
Number of joins inside the sliding window that activates raid mode.
Length in seconds of the sliding join window used for flood detection.
Minimum account age while anti-raid is enabled; younger accounts are politely turned away with a DM. Zero disables the gate.

Graduated containment stages: stage 1 turns raid-window joiners away (kick or ban with optional message-history delete seconds), stage 2 locks down — verification raised to Very High and invites paused with settings snapshotted — if the flood persists through a stage.
Automatically unban members who were banned during raid mode once the raid cools down.
Calm minutes without threshold pressure before raid mode deactivates and every containment measure auto-reverses.
Channel for raid detection, containment, and all-clear posts; empty string falls back to the mod log channel.

defaults.rationale: Lenient locked default: no join is ever gated, deferred, or tracked until the owner deliberately opts in.
Ten joins in the window is far above organic traffic for most servers, so false raid activations stay rare.
A tight ten-second window matches real raid tooling cadence without penalizing a popular invite moment.
One week filters throwaway raid accounts while barely touching genuine newcomers, who get a warm try-again-soon DM.
Graduated locked default: start with the gentlest effective measure — reversible kicks with a respectful DM — and only lock the doors if the raid keeps coming.
Member-respectful default: raid bans are containment, not permanent judgments, so they lift automatically with the all-clear.
Five calm minutes reliably outlasts raid bursts while keeping lockdown friction short for genuine members.
Raid events fall back to the mod log until the owner dedicates a channel, so no raid is ever invisible.
